steps: Sim-funded first: every firm here pays from a simulated account until its risk team moves you.
The trigger is a payout count (MFFU Builder 5, LucidPro 5, Tradeify 3-5, Bulenox 3, FundedNext 15 rewards) or a review.
Expect KYC (ID check) and a contract: a live account is real money at a broker.
Rules change: different split (Tradeify 80/20), daily payouts (MFFU, Lucid), a static floor, a reserve held back.
Some moves close or merge your other accounts (Bulenox merges, FundedNext's old structure disabled all, Tradeify: sources conflict).
Bots: Topstep bans bots on Live; MFFU requires the owner present for live and CME-compliant automation. Never arm live for the bot.
Ask in writing before accepting: what happens to my other accounts, the split, the floor, the contract cap.

rows.title: LIT losses - where and why LIT loses in 2026, and the rules worth adding
rows.summary: Every 2026 trade of LIT final was taken apart (time, level, sweep, inducement, stop, MFE, news, VIX, ES, opens, 1H/4H). 59 stop-outs carry 97% of the lost dollars. They are trades that never worked (median best point +0.3R, 45 minutes to the stop), not shake-outs. About 110 rules were tested, each picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct, plus timeframes and the masters-study filters. Two rules help both halves and the eval: a weekly stop (after 2 stop-outs in a week, half size for the rest of it) and a Monday rule (once Monday has taken Friday's high, only shorts; once it has taken Friday's low, only longs). Together (lit_loss_pack): 2026 +$41.7k, PF 3.66, max DD -$2.3k, eval pass rate 95.5% (was 80%), H1 +$2.1k and H2 +$0.75k better than LIT final. Every exit-management idea (scale-outs, trails, stop to the inducement) and every other timeframe lost money in both halves.

rows.title: LIT loss learning - the 15-minute check, and what the losses can't tell us
rows.summary: Every 2026 LIT trade was re-played on its true 1-minute path and scored on the number that matters most, the MFFU 50K 2-week pass rate under the live two-week sizing (config C). One rule holds in both halves. The 15-minute check: 15 minutes after the fill, if the trade has never been +0.5R in profit and the 1m close is more than 0.3R below the entry, get out at the next 1m open. It cut 13 trades in 2026, all of them would-be full stop-outs, at about -0.45R instead of -1R, and touched no winner. 2-week pass H1 52.9% -> 57.1% and H2 50.7% -> 52.2%; 2-week fails 8.4% -> 5.9% and 2.9% -> 0%; the Monte Carlo agrees in both halves; eval-path money +$4.4k (H1) and +$5.0k (H2). Its neighbours (0.25-0.4R, +0.3-0.7R, minute 15-20) agree. Checking earlier (5-12 min) or later (25-30 min), or keeping the check on after minute 15, kills slow winners in Jul-Oct. rows.title: LIT live fills - how the orders really fill on the MFFU account, and what that does to the numbers
rows.summary: A study of how LIT's orders fill on NinjaTrader -> Tradovate -> CME for the MFFU account, and a realistic fill model built from it (engine/lit.py option "fills", off by default). No backtest matches live exactly, so this is the most realistic model we can defend, plus a tool (tools/fill_audit.py) that measures the real fills. Order handling costs little. MFFU's $1.90 commission, stop slippage, the spread, the tick-rounded target limit and the breakeven lag together cost about $1.2k of 2026's $41.7k under the LIT size rule (+$40.5k, PF 3.48 instead of 3.66). rows.title: LIT learning loop - how the bot learns from its losses, what it may change, and what it would have learned in 2026
rows.summary: Every finished LIT trade now goes into a journal (data/lit_journal.jsonl) with its 50 entry facts, the outcome, MFE/MAE and a loss cause code. Every Sunday a review re-estimates a small set of bounded size knobs (0.5x to 1.25x per bucket, a skip only for a bucket that lost money over 15+ trades) with shrinkage toward 1.0x. Each proposed change has to pass six guardrails before it can go live, and every decision is logged and can be reverted. Replayed on 2026 with only the data before each Sunday, the learner made 3 changes, all on the inducement (trap) age, by late April: stale traps 0.5x, fresh traps 1.25x. That is the same thing the trade-selection study found by hand. It made 0 changes on 2021-25. The money was not better in both halves. H1 eval path +$3.6k but funded -$1.1k; H2 -$0.4k, and 2-week passes fell from 29.5% to 23.1%. So the loop ships in OBSERVE mode. It journals, learns

rows.title: LIT funded sizing - how big to trade once the MFFU eval is passed
rows.summary: After the MFFU Builder 50K eval passes, the goal changes from speed to payouts without losing the account. The exact live LIT trades of 2026 were replayed on a modelled MFFU funded account (EOD trailing $2,000 locking at +$100, $1,000 soft daily loss, payouts above a $2,100 buffer, $500-$2,000 a request, best day at most 50% of the cycle, 5 sim payouts, 80% split). Keeping today's normal or eval size on a funded account loses 20-22% (Jan-Jun) / 28-29% (Jul-Oct) of accounts within 6 months. The new mode "funded" risks 40% of the room to the floor (at most $800, so a fresh account trades the normal LIT size), sizes so a winner pays at most $1,500 (the 50% best-day payout rule), keeps the weekly stop, and skips a trade when even 1 micro could reach the floor. rows.title: LIT final - one LIT strategy built from the four 2026 studies
rows.summary: The four LIT studies (entry, sessions, risk, filters) were merged into one strategy and judged on 2026 only, picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct. The final, LIT final, combines the entry study's CISD entry with a 1-minute confirmation and the risk study's VIX-band target banked at 8R. In 2026 it makes +$38,873 (PF 3.06, 3.1 trades a week, max DD -$3,097), against +$20,487 for the old bot. Almost all of the extra money comes from Jan-Jun, the half the parts were tuned on. In Jul-Oct it makes +$8,212 (PF 2.19), while the old bot made +$15,568 over the same months. It only works on true 1-minute bars, most trades come in the London morning (02:00-08:00 ET), and it has no edge in 2021-25 (PF 1.03). Paper only. Since 2026-10-18 it is the paper bot's strategy (live_model.json, engine/lit_live.py; the old bot runs on as a shadow ledger).

rows.title: LIT experiments - sizing like a prop trader, a New York session, other targets, other stops, and the masters' ideas
rows.summary: About 150 variants of LIT final were tested on 2026 CME NQ1! futures (5m + 1m bars). Each was picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct, with 2021-25 as a reference. None of the strategy changes beat LIT final in both halves. That covers a New York second session, 15 target ideas, 5 stop anchors with 4 buffers, breakeven on structure, partials at liquidity, re-entries, minimum 3R and a two-stage entry. The only real gains come from sizing for the MFFU 50K eval. (1) Fast-eval size: $800 risk up to a 40-pt stop instead of 20. It passes about half of all evals within 2 weeks in both halves (H1 52% vs 33%, H2 47% vs 23%) and halves the expected time to a pass, but about 1 eval in 4 fails within 2 weeks. (2) A max-loss room cap: never risk more than 60% of the distance to the trailing max-loss floor. It cuts 2-week failures from 15% to 4% in H1 and leaves H2 unchanged. Paper only.

rows.title: LIT entry precision - can the entry be "on the dot"? Direct limit vs confirmation vs refined limit, per original setup
rows.summary: The owner asked for entries that are on the dot. 43 entry variants were run on the exact live LIT setups of 2026 (true 1m bars, costs in), picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct, scored in $ on the LIT rule and on the MFFU 50K 2-week pass rate under the live two_week sizing. A plain resting limit at the zone fills 3 setups in 4 instead of 1 in 2 and gets a better price on the trades both take, but the extra fills are the setups that never confirm, and they lose (H1 -$28.9k at $1,000 a setup). rows.title: LIT all hours - trading the whole CME day (Asia, 15:30-16:00, more trades a day, re-arming, the 18:00 F-BoS, trendline liquidity)

rows.title: LIT advanced report ch2-4 - thesis boundary, session carryover, weak reactions, ES same event, owner's session and inducement notes
rows.summary: The owner's LIT Advanced Decisions Report (chapters 2-4, experiment 4 of chapter 13) and his LIT group's session / Smart Money Trap / inducement notes became 176 variants on the 2026 LIT path, each picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct, under the live two-week eval sizing. Four variants improve both halves; three are lone points whose neighbours fail, and the best one (skip a sweep made by one huge 5m bar with no pause before it) changes only 2 trades per half. Every fixable item together (a stop bar that opened through the stop, 50 missing 1m minutes in 9 trades, the 15:55 flat clock, the early-close holidays) moves 2026 by about -$500 of +$41,734, mostly in H1. rows.summary: The owner asked for 1-minute entries and loss management that thinks like a person. On the exact live LIT signals (2026, true 1m bars, eval sizing $800 up to a 25-pt stop + the 60% room cap), 153 variants were tested, picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct. 1m entry filters (inner 1m inducement, 1m displacement, volume, absorption, patience, pullback entries) all lose money in both halves. The classic "trade is wrong" signals (1m CISD against, a new 1m low, back inside the swept level, higher low taken, a volume surge against) do cut 50-100% of the losers early, but they also kill 30-80% of the winners. rows.title: What to expect: streaks, drawdowns, flat months and the odds inside a 2-week eval
rows.summary: The locked strategy wins 1 trade in 4-5 and loses or scratches the rest, so long runs without a winner are normal: 33 trades in a row without a win happened once (Sep-Nov 2025, -$3,126), and 2026 had 16 (Apr-May, -$1,667). A loss does not make the next trade worse (after a loss +0.02R, after a win -0.01R in 2021-25, p=0.79), so sitting out or halving the trade after a max-size loss loses money in both periods (rejected). Most months lose a little (median month -$184 over 5 years, 40% of months positive; 2026 median +$1,162, 50% positive); 13 trades made the whole 5-year profit. In a 2-week eval expect 4+ non-winners in a row in about half of the starts (2021-25 58%, 2026 27%), a $1,000 dip in 12% (2026 1%), a $2,000 dip in 1%.

rows.title: VWAP and volume profile as confluence
rows.summary: None of 24 VWAP and volume-profile ideas made the live strategy better in both 2026 and 2021-25 when used to size trades up or down (every trade still taken, 2.2 and 3.2 trades a week). The only raw pass, 1.25x size on days that open inside yesterday's value area (2026 PF 3.50 vs 3.48, 2021-25 PF 1.10 vs 1.09), fails the robustness checks, so the live strategy stays as it is.

rows.title: Unexpected factors: 33 things the owner would not think of, none of them real
rows.summary: 33 unusual conditions knowable at entry (VIX / VXN / GEX / dark-pool buying, overnight and gap size, inside days, days since a 2% day, trades already this week, pre-market sweeps, sweep-to-trigger time, zone and candle sizes, relative volume, pool count, month-to-date P&L and more) were ranked on 2021-25. The best one, "the sweep extreme was made before 09:30" (125 trades, +0.159R vs -0.022R), has a t of 1.3 and a shuffle test says a random relabelling beats it 16% of the time alone and 95% of the time once you allow for 33 tries. The 1.25x size rules that "beat the baseline in both periods" do so only because they add leverage: flat 1.25x on every trade makes more (2021-25 +$18,350 vs +$17,472-17,919). Nothing to adopt.

rows.title: Trade construction: what to change before Sunday
rows.summary: One change is worth making, together with the sizing change: on trending days move the stop to breakeven at +3R instead of +1R. With the sizing change it adds +$4.8k to 2021-25 (PF 1.19 → 1.27) and changes nothing in 2026 evals; on today's sizing alone it causes extra late-May 2026 eval fails, so then keep the current rules. Stops, targets, the other exits, filters and timing are already at their best; 120+ variants tested, no leak found.

rows.title: Targets: where profits are taken
rows.summary: Today's target (nearest major pool at least 1.5R away, banking at 5R when the draw is farther) is the best of 15 variants. Nearer caps (3-4R) cut 2026 profit by $5-8k; farther caps (6-8R) help 2021-25 a little but cost 2026 $5-7k; exiting in front of the pool changes almost nothing.

rows.title: Stress tests of the locked strategy: costs, price feed, worst start, size rounding, contract caps, late fills
rows.summary: The locked strategy survives 2-tick slippage or doubled commission (2021-25 still +$13-14k, PF 1.21-1.22) but 3 ticks plus doubled commission takes 58% of its 2021-25 profit (+$6.9k, PF 1.11), and about half of every cost hit comes from the cold-streak filter flipping state on 3-26 trades. TradingView (MNQ1!) and the Python bot (NQ1!) will end a year roughly $5k apart with no bias; the fastest way to fail an eval is 7-8 full-size losers right after a good run (6-8 sessions, Feb 2023 and Nov 2024); 47% of trades are 1 micro and cost about $450 a year; a 20-micro cap costs 17% of the profit, a 10-micro cap 39%; filling one bar late loses about half of 2021-25.

rows.title: Stops: where the stop should go
rows.summary: Today's stop (2 points beyond the sweep extreme, 10-60 points) is the best of 19 variants. Wider buffers, volatility-scaled (ATR) buffers, other min/max limits and stops beyond the gap all lose money in 2026, 2021-25 or both; no stop change is recommended.

rows.title: Risk summary: size down the two kinds of trades that lose
rows.summary: Recommendation: quarter size (not half) in cold streaks and half size on late entries. Same trades: 2021-25 +$11.5k instead of +$6.5k (PF 1.19 vs 1.09, max DD -$9.2k vs -$11.4k), 2026 +$20.6k instead of +$20.1k (PF 4.12 vs 3.48), 1-month eval fails in 2021-25 9.4% to 5.1%. For the 2-week eval rule, an optional fast mode ($800 on any stop until the eval is $1,000 down) doubles eval speed at the same evals per pass but fails more evals a year.

rows.title: Risk and sizing: every sizing idea tested on both periods
rows.summary: Changing how much the bot risks per trade moves money and drawdown together and does not fix 2021-25. More risk ($1,000-1,200, or no wide-stop scaling) makes more in 2026 but doubles eval fails; less risk drops below 2 setups a week. The changes that help both periods size down specific losing trades: quarter size in cold streaks, half size on late entries.

rows.title: Parameter robustness: does the lock sit on a plateau or on a peak?
rows.summary: Mostly a plateau, with one ridge. Cold size, late size, the trending-day breakeven (anything from +3R to never gives the same money), the $ risk and the wide-stop rule all move smoothly. The exception is the cold-streak lookback of 15 signals: 15 and 16 give +$16.4k / +$16.9k in 2021-25, but 14 gives +$13.3k, 13 gives +$7.8k and 17 gives +$10.7k, so about half of the 5-year gain over the morning rules (+$6.5k) depends on that one number. Every one of 105 neighbouring combinations stays profitable in both periods (2021-25 worst +$6.8k, 2026 worst +$19.6k). The lock has 17 of 55 rolling 6-month windows negative (morning rules 22) and a longest flat stretch of 68 weeks (85).

rows.title: Moving averages as confluence
rows.summary: The textbook "trade with the EMA trend" filters all cost money (2026 net falls by $5-8k). The one moving-average fact that helps is a warning sign: when price is 3+ hourly ATRs on the wrong side of the 1-hour EMA 20 (a "falling knife"), trading at half size lifts 2021-25 from +$6.5k to +$9.6k (+$127 to +$189 a month, PF 1.09 to 1.13, 1-month eval fails 9.4% to 6.2%) while 2026 is unchanged (+$20.1k, PF 3.49), with every setup still traded.

rows.title: Monte Carlo of the MFFU 50K eval: how often, how fast, how many evals
rows.summary: One 50K eval on the locked strategy has about a 35% chance of passing within 60 sessions, 30% of failing and 35% of still running (the real history says 41 / 22 / 37); a typical pass takes 28 sessions, and a funded account costs 1.9 evals and about 5.5 months of fees (roughly $840 at list price), median 15 weeks. Starting the eval during a cold streak cuts the 1-month pass odds from 22% to 4%, so time the purchase to the filter. The fast press gets funded in a median 9.8 weeks for 3.7 months of fees but fails half of its evals.

rows.title: Managing the trade: breakeven, locks, time stop, giveback
rows.summary: Today's management is at its sweet spot on all-days rules, with one exception: on trending days (10-day efficiency above 0.45) waiting until +3R to move to breakeven adds +$4.7k to 2021-25 (PF 1.09 → 1.15) and leaves 2026 net unchanged (+$20.1k). On today's sizing it adds some late-May 2026 eval fails (beyond 1 month); with the sizing research's quarter size in cold streaks it is clean (+$4.8k in 2021-25). Profit locks, other time stops and giveback levels all lose.

rows.title: Cutting losses to pass more MFFU evals: what works, and how high the pass rate can go
rows.summary: No loss-cut rule makes a big, proven difference. The best new idea, half size for the rest of the eval week after two losing trades in that week, lifts the pass rate of decided evals from 40% to 42% (2021-25) and 53% to 56% (5 years), makes a little more money in both periods (2026 +$289, 2021-25 +$828) and cuts 2021-25 1-month fails from 5.2% to 3.1%. Its neighbours agree, but the trades it shrinks are not worse than average, so it is a small safety rule, not an edge. The intraday package does not survive the critic: CISD x1.25 lowers the pass rate, and the 30-40 pt and equal-highs slices flip by year or by odd/even month. The math: with a 21% win rate, a +$542 average win and a -$114 average loss, 2021-25 passes about 40% of decided evals at today's size. 70-80% is only reachable in a 2026-like market (91% today), or by trading so small that one eval takes 6-12 months.

rows.title: Loss anatomy: where the money leaks
rows.summary: In 2021-25 the losses gave back 92% of what the winners made (285R won, 287R lost). The leaks are long cold streaks, not big single losses (the worst day is -$875). Full stop-outs are 80% of the money lost, and trades taken in a cold streak lost money in both periods.

rows.title: Leakage check: does the backtest peek at the future?
rows.summary: No leak. Switching off the trade memory (memory_seed) and the exit learner (exit_learn) gives exactly the same 768 trades as the live strategy, so every result in this research is leak-free as it stands.

rows.title: Intraday anatomy: when, how and where the bot's trades make or lose money
rows.summary: The clock does not decide the trade (every hour and weekday flips between 2026 and 2021-25); what the trade is made of does. CISD triggers beat IFVG triggers in both periods (2026 PF 5.7 vs 2.4, 2021-25 PF 1.53 vs 1.11), 30-40 pt stops and equal-highs/lows targets lose money in both. Halving the 30-40 pt stops is the one clean small win (2026 +$413, 2021-25 +$115, max drawdown -$9.3k to -$8.1k, 1-month eval fails 5.2% to 4.0%); adding CISD x1.25 and half size on equal-highs targets makes 2026 +$3.7k and 2021-25 +$1.4k with less drawdown in both, but it is three in-sample slices stacked, so it needs a critic before Sunday.

rows.title: Eval sizing: can the eval's own state pass more MFFU evals?
rows.summary: Sizing from the eval's state (cushion above the trailing max loss, profit, distance to the target) cuts eval fails a lot (2021-25 1-month fails 9.4% to 0.3-2%), but it also passes fewer evals a year and leaves 43-60% of evals stuck after 3 months, and the result depends on the exact threshold. None beats fixed sizing robustly; the recommended cold-streak / late-entry sizing improves evals more (2.63 evals bought per pass in 2021-25 vs 3.89). For the owner's 2-week rule see the fast mode in risk-summary.md.

rows.title: The eval game: which plan, when to start, two accounts, after a fail, and the road to the first payout
rows.summary: The MFFU Builder 50K is the right eval for this strategy (1.24 evals per pass in 2026, 2.52 in 2021-25, about $313 / $1,006 of fees per funded account); the $1.5k add-on fails twice as often, plans with a best-day rule in the eval take 2-17 months, and the best moment to start is right after the cold-streak filter switches back to full size (2021-25 pass within a month 26% vs 9% overall, 2% in a cold streak). A second account on the same trades buys no speed, after a fail the next pass takes a median 3.3 months, and once funded the first payout takes 3.3 (2026) / 7.7 (2021-25) months if MFFU's 50% best-day rule applies at payout (1.3 / 1.7 months if not) while 21% / 58% of funded accounts hit the trailing loss before any payout.

rows.title: Cross-market and regime context: does the market around the setup matter?
rows.summary: Mostly no. VIX level and change, the VXN/VIX ratio, dealer gamma (GEX), NQ-vs-ES relative strength, SMT divergence and the shape of the entry day do not split trades in a way that holds in both 2026 and 2021-25; 25 of 32 size rules were rejected. One small thing does hold: when BOTH the 10-day and the 20-day trend reading say "trending" (12 trades in 2026, 75 in 2021-25), the reversal loses money in every period; half size there adds +$378 in 2026 (PF 3.94 to 4.16, drawdown -$2,249 to -$1,871) and +$677 in 2021-25 (PF 1.27 to 1.29). The bigger lead is that the 20-day trend test picks the bad days better than the live 10-day test (swap: 2026 +$2.1k, 2021-25 +$5.6k, but more 1-month eval fails); it needs an engine option and a longer live data window before it can be tested exactly.

rows.title: Calendar and seasonality: does the date matter?
rows.summary: No. Across 36 calendar factors (weekday, month, month turn, holidays, OPEX, FOMC/CPI/NFP days, DST and roll weeks, first trade of the week) nothing holds in both 2026 and 2021-25 beyond what chance produces. The only rule that is better in both periods, half size the day after NFP, gains $748 over 5 years and $256 in 2026 on 3 trades; a random group of the same size does as well 15% of the time. Keep trading every day at the normal size.

rows.title: Bias, filters and timing: which trades to take, and how big
rows.summary: Two simple biases separate trades in both periods: fading yesterday's candle and trading on the side of last week's midpoint. As filters or score points they cut trades below 2 a week and the replacement trades lose; as a size-down (70% size when both disagree) they raise PF in both periods (2026 3.48 → 3.62, 2021-25 1.09 → 1.12) and cut 2021-25 drawdown, for −$0.75k in 2026. No filter or timing change beats today's rules.

steps.title: Mark the liquidity first
steps.text: The bot keeps a list of levels that exist *before* anything happens: the Asia, London and New York session highs and lows (a box counts only after its last candle closed), the previous day, week and month high and low, the weekly and daily opening gaps, and "equal lows" (two 5m swing lows at the same price, untouched in between).

steps.title: Wait for a sweep
steps.text: Price makes a new 2-hour low and, on the way, trades through a level nobody had touched yet. It has to go at least half an ATR past it.

steps.title: Check the inducement
steps.text: Before the sweep, a small 5m swing low sat a little above the level (within 1 ATR, at most 3 hours old). The final push ran through it: the early buyers got stopped. That trapped group is the "inducement".

steps.title: Wait for the shift (5m CISD)
steps.text: Take the run of down-close 5m candles into the low; its first candle's open is the CISD level. The trigger is the first 5m close above it. Somewhere between the low and the trigger, one candle body must be at least 0.8 ATR (displacement).

steps.title: Place the order
steps.text: A buy limit at the CISD level, valid for 30 minutes. Entries only from 02:00 to 15:30.

steps.title: Confirm on 1 minute
steps.text: When price taps the limit, the bot waits up to 20 one-minute candles for a 1m CISD (a 1m close back above the open of the last run of 1m down-closes), then buys at the next 1m open.

steps.title: Stop
steps.text: 1 tick beyond the sweep low. Never a fixed distance. A planned stop under 8 or over 80 points means no trade.

steps.title: Target
steps.text: the 18:00 open plus one VIX one-day move (the "VIX band"). It must be at least 1.5R away; if it is more than 8R away, profit is taken at 8R.

steps.title: Manage
steps.text: stop to breakeven at +1R, flat by 15:55, one trade a day.

steps.title: Size
steps.text: $800 risk up to a 20-point stop, then 800 x 20 / stop (a wider stop = fewer micros). After 2 stop-outs in a week, half size for the rest of that week. On Mondays, once Friday's high is taken only shorts, once Friday's low is taken only longs.

clocks: **New York time with a named time zone** (America/New_York), never a fixed UTC offset. Bars are stored in UTC.
**Trading day 18:00 to 17:00**; the CME daily halt is 17:00-18:00 ET and Friday has no evening session.

**Early closes:** US holiday sessions halt at 13:00 ET; the day after Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve at 13:15 ET; Good Friday 09:15 ET when it trades. Since 2026-10-18 the NinjaTrader route stops new entries 15 minutes and flattens 5 minutes before such a halt (before, it would have held a position into a holiday close).

**Daylight saving:** the US and Europe change clocks on different dates. In 2026, Mar 9-27 and Oct 26-30 the London open is 04:00 ET instead of 03:00. The bot's London boxes are New York windows (03:00-04:00 ET all year); the Berlin-time version was tested (`lit-report-tests`).
**The old 16:15-16:30 pause no longer exists** for NQ/MNQ (removed by CME in June 2021).
one_minute: What LIT is: a way to read a chart. Obvious highs and lows attract orders (stops, breakout entries). Price often runs through such a level, traps the traders who reacted to it, and then turns. LIT tries to trade that turn.

What the report insists on: LIT is a set of ideas to test, not a proof. A sweep (price running through a level) can turn into a reversal, a breakout that keeps going, or a range. Only rules that are written before the trade, and then tested with real costs, can show an edge.

What the bot does: one fixed version of LIT, written as exact rules (below). Every number in it was picked on Jan-Jun 2026 and checked on Jul-Oct 2026. Results: 2026 +$41,734 (PF 3.66, 2.9 trades a week), Jul-Oct alone +$8,962 (about $2,400 a month, the rate to expect).

What the report added: 16 new rule ideas (44 variants) were tested on 2026 (`lit-report-tests`). None improved both halves of 2026 in a way that holds up, so the rules did not change. Four execution fixes from the report's last two chapters went into the bot's plumbing (order states, early closes, the paper ledger).
